diseases.disease_name: Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot / Blackarm
symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots bounded by leaf veinlets; lesions turn brown to black; blackarm lesion girdles branches; circular water-soaked sunken spots on bolls.
management: Consult local agricultural university / KVK package of practices for registered treatment.
prevention: Practice crop rotation, field hygiene, and use certified seeds.

symptoms: Yellowing and browning along leaf margins extending inwards; wilting starts from lower leaves upwards; dark brown vascular discoloration inside peeled taproot.
management: Consult local agricultural university / KVK package of practices for registered treatment.
prevention: Practice crop rotation, field hygiene, and use certified seeds.

symptoms: Angular water-soaked lesions on leaves delimited by veins
Lesions turn dark brown to black over time
Blackarm symptoms on stems and petiole wilting
management: Spray copper oxychloride (50 WP) @ 2.5 g/L plus Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L
Remove and destroy heavily infested crop residues
prevention: Delint and treat seeds with Carbendazim or carboxin prior to sowing
Adopt resistant or tolerant cotton cultivars
Follow crop rotation with non-host crops like cereals

symptoms: Upward or downward curling of leaf margins
Thickening and enation (leaf-like outgrowths) on leaf undersides
Severe plant stunting and reduced boll production
management: Manage whitefly vector with systemic insecticides (Diafenthiuron or Acetamiprid)
Uproot and bury severely infected stunted plants
Eradicate alternate weed hosts in and around fields
prevention: Install yellow sticky traps (10-15 per acre) to monitor and control whiteflies
Avoid sowing near tobacco or ladyfinger fields

diseases.disease_name: Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum)
symptoms: Yellowing and wilting of leaves starting from the bottom upward
Dark brown to black vascular discoloration inside the taproot and stem
Stunting and premature death of plants
management: Drench root zone with Carbendazim (1 g/L) or Trichoderma viride formulation
Apply balanced potash nutrition to boost disease resistance
prevention: Soil solarization during hot summer months
Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4-6 g/kg seed
Practice minimum 3-year crop rotation with non-susceptible crops

management: Maintain regular irrigation schedule without water stagnation
Apply recommended NPK and micronutrient dosage as per soil test
Monitor weekly for pest scouts (bollworms, aphids, thrips)
prevention: Continue balanced soil and plant health management
Ensure adequate border vegetation for beneficial predator insects

symptoms: Rosetted flower buds; larvae bore into young bolls, feeding on seeds and staining lint; premature boll opening.
management: Install Gossyplure pheromone traps @ 5/acre for monitoring (8/trap/day = ETL); spray Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.8ml/L or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.5g/L.

symptoms: Chlorotic stippling on leaf surface; severe honeydew secretion resulting in black sooty mold; vector of Cotton Leaf Curl Virus.
management: Spray Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2g/L or Pyriproxyfen 10% EC @ 2ml/L; spray neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 2ml/L.

correction: Foliar spray of Potassium Nitrate (13:0:45) @ 10g/L or SOP (0:0:50) @ 10g/L at weekly intervals during boll development.

healthy_signs: Robust, thick cane stalks or deep-lobed green leaves with vigorous growth
Strong internodes free from boreholes or internal red rot
Clean foliar canopy with active photosynthesis
Sturdy root anchoring with no basal wilt
management: Uproot and burn severely wilted or red-rot infected canes/plants immediately
Drench border rows with biocontrol formulations to create protective barrier zones
Follow integrated pest management (IPM) guidelines strictly
prevention: Select healthy setts/seeds from certified nurseries or disease-free mother plants
Adopt drip irrigation to avoid excess soil moisture around root crowns
Practice deep summer ploughing to expose soil-borne resting spores and pupae
Rotate with green manure crops such as sunnhemp or daincha
